title: Load Shepherd runtime protocol — scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Short scratchpad for an edge-friendly runtime coordination protocol (working name: Load Shepherd). Goal: give ingress/frontends a lightweight, observable way to steer request placement, prefetch warmups and temporary admission control across many small runtime shards while preserving low tail latency and predictable cost.

Principles:
- leases over locks: runtime nodes claim short-lived leases for request windows rather than exclusive locks; enables fast failover.
- credit-aware admission: frontends track per-shard token credits instead of queue lengths to reduce overcommit during bursts.
- probe/steer hooks: run-time exposes small probing endpoints to check warmness, KV cache hit rate, and dominant sequence-length distribution.
- eventual consistency: optimistic decisions are allowed; shepherd reconciles state periodically.

Actors and components:
- Frontend (ingress) — attempts to schedule requests across candidate shards.
- Runtime shard (sheep) — serves requests; exposes shepherd-sidecar endpoints.
- Shepherd controller (optional central view) — aggregates telemetry, suggests rebalances and blacklist lists; can be hosted or colocated with frontends.

Control-plane endpoints (sidecar on runtime shard) - HTTP/1.1 JSON API (small payloads):
- POST /lease/claim
  request: {"frontend_id": "str", "window_ms": 200, "expected_tokens": 120, "priority": "p0|p1|p2", "call_id": "uuid"}
  response: {"lease_id": "uuid", "granted_tokens": 100, "expires_at": "iso_ts", "accepted_sequence_hint": 256}
  notes: if not enough capacity, return 409 with backfill hint.

- POST /lease/release
  request: {"lease_id": "uuid", "used": 54, "skipped": 0}
  response: {"ok": true, "returned_tokens": 46}

- POST /probe/warmth
  request: {"call_id": "uuid", "path_hint": "/generate", "probe_budget": 10}
  response: {"kv_hit_rate": 0.72, "active_kv_entries": 1223, "avg_decoding_ms": 5}

- GET /metrics/score
  returns: {"score": 0..1 , "reason": "prefetch-able | busy | cold | degraded"}

- POST /steer/signal
  request: {"directive": "drain|drain_soft|promote|demote", "until": "iso_ts", "reason": "string"}
  response: {"ack": true}

API shapes above intentionally minimal to keep sidecar small (few fields, no nested objects other than flat structs). We prefer "granted_tokens" semantics for quick admission. Frontend summation of granted_tokens across shards forms admission budget.

Lease semantics and invariants:
- max lease window: 1000ms (configurable).
- tokens decrement on request admission; runtime returns unused tokens on release.
- expired lease doesn't automatically revert token usage — runtime reconciles during heartbeat.
- frontends should retry claim with exponential backoff and jitter on 5xx or 409; consider local fallback policy (pin to cached shard) after 3 failed claims.

Config knobs (frontends + sidecar):
- token_unit: default = 1 per 16 tokens (approx 16 model tokens) — tune by model and batch size.
- soft_threshold_pct: 0.65 — below this take probe before claim.
- hard_threshold_pct: 0.9 — reject new leases when exceeded.
- probe_interval_ms: 2000 — how often frontends probe a cold shard.
- lease_ttl_ms: 300 — default small window to reduce contention.
- reconcile_interval_ms: 15000 — shepherd controller reconcile frequency.

Telemetry model (events):
- lease_acquired: {frontend_id, shard_id, lease_id, granted_tokens, window_ms, call_id}
- lease_released: {lease_id, used, returned_tokens}
- probe_result: {shard_id, kv_hit_rate, avg_decode_ms}
- steer_applied: {shard_id, directive}

All telemetry should include a small span_id and optional debug stack to trace decisions for postmortems. Keep payload size < 1KB per event.

Sequence diagram (ASCII):
  Frontend -> Shard : POST /lease/claim (expected_tokens=80)
  Shard --> Frontend : 200 {granted_tokens=60, lease_id}
  Frontend -> Shard : send 3 parallel requests (consume 60 tokens)
  Frontend -> Shard : POST /lease/release (used=50)
  Shard --> Frontend : 200 {returned_tokens=10}
  Shepherd -> Frontend : (optional) /steer/signal drain_soft on shard-7

Failure modes & heuristics:
- Cold-start false negatives: if probe returns kv_hit_rate < 0.1 but avg_decoding small, treat as transient.
- Token leak on crash: runtime upon restart broadcasts /metrics/score=0 and shepherd triggers soft-drain.
- Network partitions: leases expire; frontends must have local fallback; avoid global blocking operations.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should leases be signed tokens (HMAC) so frontends can't misreport? (pro: tamper-proof; con: compute cost).
- How to reconcile with existing batching engine's local admission? Do we expose internal queue length metric or keep only token model?
- Backpressure propagation across multi-hop frontends: simple hop-by-hop or propagate root cause?
- Cost accounting: map granted_tokens to billing units — simpler if 1:1 to token accounting but may diverge with batching.

Mini experiments to run:
- Synthetic workload with 10k RPS across 200 shards, compare 3 admission models: naive round-robin, token-lease, central shepherd. Metrics: tail latency (p99.9), request drop rate, wasted warmup probes.
- Measure HMAC overhead for signed leases at 50k claims/sec.

Next immediate steps (owners):
- (Ava) draft a tiny sidecar prototyping server (Go) with claim/release/probe endpoints.
- (Marco) add a sim harness in dist-sim to model token leak/crash recovery.
- (Priya) write an experiment design doc for the 3-way scheduler comparison.

Notes to self: keep API surfaces dumb and telemetry rich. The runtime-sidecar should be O(1) memory per lease and O(1) CPU for common paths. Avoid nested JSONs in API responses to keep parsing cheap in frontends (node/Go).

References / inspiration:
- admission-control token buckets (generalized)
- short-leases from k8s leader election pattern
- speculative prefetching literature (shadow prewarm techniques)

End of scratchpad.
